title: Submerge an ice cooling paddle into a commercial stockpot of hot soup, agitate to chill, and hang the paddle on the rim bracket
instruction: Steady the stockpot handle, pick up the frozen cooling paddle from the stand, immerse it into the hot soup, agitate in circular revolutions to chill the broth, lift to drain, and hang the paddle securely on the rim bracket. Move both hands clear.
context: Restaurant cooks (O*NET 35-2014.00, 1,440,000 US jobs) and food preparation workers (35-2021.00, 891,000 US jobs) must rapidly cool large stockpots of cooked soups, stocks, and sauces under FDA Food Code 3-501.14 (cooling from 135°F to 70°F within 2 hours, and down to 41°F within 4 hours to prevent spore germination of Clostridium perfringens and Bacillus cereus). Leaving deep pots to cool passively fails safety limits. Staff use hollow polyethylene ice cooling wands (e.g. San Jamar Rapi-Kool, Carlisle Coldmaster) filled with frozen core water. The cook retrieves the heavy frozen paddle from its stand, submerges the finned blade deep into the hot broth, agitates with circular stirring strokes to circulate liquid around the cold fins without splashing boiling liquid over the rim, raises the paddle to allow broth to drain back into the pot, and hooks the integrated collar hook onto the pot rim bracket so the paddle stays suspended.
setup: Station prep counter (Z=0.7475 m, coordinates in metres from arm-base midpoint). Center: 16 qt heavy-gauge stainless stockpot (260 mm OD, 240 mm ID, 130 mm tall, 2.8 kg) on silicone heat mat at (0.260, 0.080), containing 8 L broth simulant (depth 70 mm, surface Z=0.8285 m, 54 mm headspace to rim). Front-left pot rim features a welded stainless paddle hanging bracket with an 18 mm horizontal resting saddle at (0.240, 0.180, Z=0.8825 m). Right pot side has a heavy loop handle at (0.260, -0.060, Z=0.8205 m). Left counter: stainless sanitary paddle stand (120x120x50 mm, 600 g) at (0.220, 0.220) with a vertical 40 mm deep cradle. Commercial ice paddle (San Jamar Rapi-Kool style): 650 g HDPE wand, 110x60x32 mm finned blade, 25 mm collar with radial hanging hook extending 30 mm, and 65 mm cylindrical grip handle (dia 28 mm). Paddle starts standing upright in cradle (blade bottom Z=0.7575 m, handle grip center Z=0.9175 m). Right arm steadies pot handle while left arm transfers, stirs, and hangs paddle.
scoring: Real-world inspection: manual inspection of 5 complete circular paddle revolutions (R=35 mm) around pot centerline with wireless immersion probe logging, perimeter absorbent tray check for zero liquid overflow (<20 mL splash loss), and 10 N downward retention test on the rim bracket. Scored stages: 0.15: paddle grasped and lifted clear of stand (>35 mm); 0.35: paddle submerged into stockpot broth (depth >=45 mm); 0.60: fluid agitation achieved (>=3 circular revolutions around pot axis, cumulative angle >=6 pi rad); 0.80: agitation completed (>=5 revolutions) and paddle lifted above broth to drain position; 1.00: paddle hanging hook securely seated on rim bracket, both robot hands clear (TCPs >=30 mm, hulls >=5 mm), paddle stable for 1.0 s. Possible scores: 0, 0.15, 0.35, 0.60, 0.80, 1.00. Anti-cheat latches 0 on liquid splash (>0.45 m/s submerged velocity), dropped paddle, pot slip/tilt, or premature hook hang without agitation.
reset_notes: Drain and wipe stockpot; refill 8 L fresh broth simulant to 70 mm level. Return ice paddle to frozen storage stand at (0.220, 0.220) blade down. Reset pot to heat mat alignment at (0.260, 0.080).
fidelity: Rigid bodies and composite octagonal shapes. Broth volume is represented as a rigid bath with immersion depth and kinematic angular phase accounting tracking paddle revolutions in lieu of runtime SPH/CFD; submerged paddle velocity (>0.45 m/s) and jerk monitor splash overflow. Rim bracket hook engagement simulated via geometric seat and catch retention. Robot collision boxes checked for release clearance.
scores: Dream-1: 0.0; scripted demo: 1.0 (two complete runs, 534 steps each).
